name: The Censers of Ash
summary: The order's namesake: every sworn Censer bearer carries a censer filled with ash from the Colleges of the Weave, burned in the Sundering's aftermath. The ash is not symbolic — incense-bearers claim it remembers smoke, and that a censer swung near working magic shows a grey flame no one else can see. New members are inducted with ash from their predecessor's censer; the original Colleges' supply was rationed across eight centuries and is now nearly spent.
origin: 1 Sun (winter) — the First Censer's oath in Velkash's broken thread-quarter
current_whereabouts: Carried by every sworn member; the mother-censers (nine of them, one per Ash) rest in the archive-quarter's oath-vault.
properties: Grey flame visible only to the sworn when Glimmer-workings burn nearby — the order's oldest detection method
Induction transfers a pinch of ash; each censer's lineage is traceable back through bearers to 1 Sun
The remaining original ash would fill, at most, three censers
keepers: The Nine Ashes hold the mother-censers; running out of original ash is the order's quietest institutional crisis.
value_or_danger: To the order: irreplaceable identity. To everyone else: proof that the Censer's authority is a finite resource.
adventure_hooks: A censer is stolen — the first theft in order history. Inside job or Mile forgery run?
A First-Heard member refuses induction ash, proposing new ash 'from what we burn next'. The schism turns ritual.
Players are hired to authenticate a claimed pre-Sundering relic: a censer of College ash older than the order itself.
